after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A bag contains $4$ five-dollar bills, $8$ ten-dollar bills, and $6$ twenty-dollar bills. If one bill is randomly drawn from a bag, what is its expected value?
after.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Let $X$ be the value of a randomly drawn bill. Then the support is $S={5,10,20}.$

In the bag there are  $4$ five-dollar bills, $8$ ten-dollar bills and $6$ twenty-dollar bills (eighteen bills in total), so the probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5) & =\frac{4}{18}=\frac{2}{9} \\ P(10) & =\frac{8}{18}=\frac{4}{9} \\ P(20) & =\frac{6}{18}=\frac{3}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =5\cdot f(5)+10\cdot f(10)+20\cdot f(20) \\  & =5(\frac{2}{9})+10(\frac{4}{9})+20(\frac{3}{9}) \\  & =\frac{10}{9}+\frac{40}{9}+\frac{60}{9} \\  & =\frac{10+40+60}{9} \\  & =\frac{110}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the outcomes of rolling two fair tetrahedral dice follows the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. What is the expected value of one roll of the two dice?

| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ |

content.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6)+7\cdot f(7)+8\cdot f(8) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{16})+3(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{3}{16})+5(\frac{1}{4})+6(\frac{3}{16})+7(\frac{1}{8})+8(\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{2}{16}+\frac{3}{8}+\frac{12}{16}+\frac{5}{4}+\frac{18}{16}+\frac{7}{8}+\frac{8}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}+\frac{3}{8}+\frac{6}{8}+\frac{10}{8}+\frac{9}{8}+\frac{7}{8}+\frac{4}{8} \\  & =\frac{1+3+6+10+9+7+4}{8} \\  & =\frac{40}{8} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Let $X$ be the value labeled on a randomly drawn card. Then the support is $S={3,6}.$

In the stack there are $8$ cards labeled with three and $4$ cards labeled with six (twelve cards in total), so the probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3) & =\frac{8}{12}=\frac{2}{3} \\ P(6) & =\frac{4}{12}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =3\cdot f(3)+6\cdot f(6) \\  & =3(\frac{2}{3})+6(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =2+2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let $p$ represent the profit on a single roll of the game. On each roll in the game, there are two possible outcomes:

- If the sum of the outcomes is $6$ ($(1,5),(2,4),(3,3),(4,2)$, or $(5,1)$), the player wins $$6,$ so we have $p=6.$

- If the sum of the outcomes is not $6,$ the player loses $$1,$ so we have $p=-1.$

The probabilities for the outcomes are

$$
P(6)=\frac{5}{36},\,P(-1)=\frac{31}{36}.

40\cdot \text{E}[W]=40\cdot 1.5=60.
